# A. Sequence Cut And Paste

## How to find it

Represent positions by subtree sizes and express removal/insertion through split and merge.

## Correctness

Split preserves in-order order on both sides and merge concatenates its operands. The four operations therefore remove precisely `[l,r]` and insert that unchanged block at the requested remaining position.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# B. Reversible Range Ledger

## How to find it

Attach whole-subtree addition and reversal tags to an implicit treap.

## Correctness

Each tag has exactly the stated effect on the stored aggregate; pushing composes it into both children before structural inspection, and pulling restores the parent invariant.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# C. Dynamic Forest XOR

## How to find it

Expose each represented path with `makeroot(u); access(v)` and aggregate its auxiliary tree.

## Correctness

After exposure, the auxiliary subtree rooted at `v` contains exactly the u-v path in order. XOR is associative and reversal-independent, so its stored aggregate is the answer.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# D. Threshold Component Size

## How to find it

Kruskal creates a new parent whenever two components merge; label it with the edge weight and component size.

## Correctness

Ancestors of a leaf are exactly its successive Kruskal components in nondecreasing threshold order. The highest ancestor of weight at most x is therefore precisely the requested component.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# Upsolving and stress testing

For A/B, maintain a literal Python-style list and apply every cut, paste,
reverse, and addition directly. For C, maintain the represented forest as
adjacency sets and reconstruct each path with BFS. For D, replay all edges up
to the queried threshold and run DSU from scratch.

Adversarial sequences should repeatedly reverse overlapping intervals, compose
updates before any query forces a push, link and cut the same edge, query a
single vertex, and use equal reconstruction thresholds. The central invariant
is always which order or tree is represented; randomized storage and preferred
paths are implementation details.
